reason: Defs/Part5.lean:19-50 states canonical examples (A), (B1), and (B2) for the fixed labelled observation, with correct supports, counts, normalized masses, common observation, excluded swap, and inclusive tails in both directions. It does not quantify over an arbitrary original 60-treated observation or construct its relabelling into the chosen normal form. Challenge/Part1.lean:12-15 expressly discloses that omission. The fixed y vectors correctly represent assignment-independent circle outcomes; no empirical Uganda percentile or p-value is asserted. The statement proves the canonical nonidentification examples rather than contradicting the canonical counterexample claim.

Defs/Part5.lean:53-88 correctly gives exact finite-law and conditional-law calibration, the independent common-Bernoulli count-conditioned probabilities, a meaningful cumulative spatial statistic and its sharp-null imputability on positive conditional support, and both four-node discrepancies. The spatial clause specializes to Euclidean circles and assumes integrability even at assignments outside positive conditional support. Its explicit conclusion is cumulative-statistic imputability, rather than separate invariance of every circle mean. The theorem omits the documented seven-lottery design, its identification with the application reference law, and the withdrawal/reanalysis conclusion. These scope limits are disclosed at Challenge/Part1.lean:23-30. Positive circle masses and both arms exclude undefined averages and ratios; the usual measurability and integrability conditions alone are not substantive restrictions.

Defs/Part5.lean:91-126 constructs exactly the canonical counterexample: four separated nodes and containing rectangle, assignment-independent outcomes, all six two-of-four assignments with their uniform law, the independent-Bernoulli conditional-law identity, positive finite integrable circle averages (0,1,2,3), five specified radii, sorted statistics, type-7 endpoints, strict rejection at exactly the two extremes, and single-radius and cumulative rejection probability 1/3 > 1/20. The finite atomic measure is a suitable counting measure; every relevant outcome is constant on its entire geometric circle, so it does not change the canonical averages. The theorem establishes the canonical counterexample; it does not refute that canonical assertion or a different quantile convention.

Defs/Part5.lean:129-153 retains canonical (a), (b), and (d), with the complement pairing, every finite weighted linear functional, lower inclusive-tail bound 1/3, every nonempty deterministic rejection-set obstruction, exact calibration for every finite design law, and the product-mass hypothesis making all B+1 observed/reference coordinates independent draws from the same law. It also retains the displayed five-estimate sum 7.996 from (c). It omits the actual unrounded/rounded observed statistic, the particular six reconstructed cumulative values and exact observed p-value, and a repetition of T3's interpolation counterexample; Challenge/Part1.lean:44-49 says so. The audit-history note is not used to erase those omitted assertions from the canonical statement.

Defs/Part6.lean:19-90 renders the canonical two-node counting-field example (including the expressly allowed addition of the nodes), independent fair-bit design, own-treatment means, actual linearization contributions, means/variances/covariance, AMR one, geometric cutoff-one covariance sum, and the entire positive-M replication with bounded outcomes, separated nodes and at-most-two-assignment circle dependence. Uniformity on the full Boolean function type gives independent assignments across pairs. Its covariance sums concern linearization variance, not an undefined finite-sample ratio estimator. The only omitted asymptotic assertion is expressly optional in the canonical statement. The docstring correctly limits the counterexample to the outcome-effect-range reading and does not call the printed dependence instruction false.
